newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tax seen as obstacle to IMF Russia disbursement.
newsitem.headline: Tax seen as obstacle to IMF Russia disbursement.

text.p: Low Russian tax revenues are still a major obstacle to a resumption of payments by the International Monetary Fund of its loan to Russia, a source familiar with talks between Russia and the IMF said on Thursday.

But the fund may decide, when its board meets in mid-May, to release some of the hundreds of millions of dollars it has withheld this year as a gesture of support to the new reformist cabinet, the source said.
No one was available to comment at the IMF office in Moscow.
Asked if the IMF would pay delayed tranches of the loan, the source said: "The tax position continues to be a major problem...the tax side is really pretty awful."

An IMF mission will visit Moscow for talks from April 23 to 25 for talks on the current state of the economy, which could clear the way to releasing some of the delayed money, and an economic programme for 1997 to be backed by the three-year $10 billion loan agreed in February 1996.
